chunks.text:
treatment of
pneumonia, hypertension, diabetes, and arthritis [2,3]. Previous phytochemical studies
revealed that M. alba contained a variety of polyphenolic constituents such as prenylated
flavonoids, 2-arylbenzofurans, stilbene, coumarin, and mulberry Diels–Alder-type adducts.
In addition, pharmacological studies exhibited that some polyphenols from M. alba had
a broad spectrum of biological activities, such as hepatoprotective activity, whitening
ability, and antiplatelet effects [4–9]. Previous studies also showed that diverse individual

compounds or extracts from different parts of various mulberry plants (M. alba, M. australis,
M. wittiorum, and M. yunanensis) exhibited anti-tumor activity against different tumor cell
lines, such as lung cancer, liver cancer, colon cancer, breast cancer, rectal adenocarcinoma,
and renal adenocarcinoma [10–14]. Our preliminary pharmacological experiment showed
that the 75% ethanol extract of M. alba exhibited certain anti-tumor activity against gastric

that the 75% ethanol extract of M. alba exhibited certain anti-tumor activity against gastric
cancer cells, which had rarely been reported. Thus, the present paper focuses on detailed
phytochemical investigation of the 75% ethanol extract of M. alba and evaluation of anti-
tumor activity against gastric cancer cells of the isolated individual compounds. As a result,
thirty-five compounds including three new ones were obtained. Among them, compound
10 (Albanol B) shows the most significant cytotoxicity with an IC50 value of 6.08 ± 0.34 µM.

摘
要：中药材从种植到流通市场的周期较长，源头或过程控制不当极易感染真菌毒素，极大地影响中药材
的品质与安全。系统检测并评估中药材的真菌毒素污染情况和潜在风险，对进一步完善中药的安全性质量控
制标准和保障其食药用安全具有重要意义。但中药材中大量的代谢产物对微痕量真菌毒素检测存在极大的基
质干扰，加之真菌毒素污染的不确定性和其结构类型的复杂性，建立广谱适用于复杂中药材基质的真菌毒素
高通量检测方法面临巨大挑战。该文对基于液相色谱-质谱联用技术（LC-MS/MS）的真菌毒素高通量检测研究

中药材在种植、采收、加工、运输、储藏等环节中，由于源头或过程控制不当极易感染真菌毒素，
极大地影响中药材的品质与安全
［6］。例如种子、块茎类中药材由于含有丰富的油脂和淀粉类物质，易
被AFs 污染；养殖动物类中药材由于富含蛋白质和脂肪等物质，易被AFs、DON、FBs 等污染
［7］。2025
年版《中国药典》对大枣、水蛭、地龙、肉豆蔻、全蝎、决明子、麦芽、远志等24种中药材制定了黄曲
霉毒素的限量标准，规定AFB1不得超过5 μg/kg，AFB1、AFB2、AFG1、AFG2总量不得超过10 μg/kg；
另外，规定了薏苡仁中ZEN 不得超过500 μg/kg，并新增黄芪和槟榔中赭曲霉毒素A（OTA）的限量为20
μg/kg
［8］。除了上述常见真菌毒素外，周恒等
［9］对涉及100余品种的3 000多批中药材和饮片进行了多种
真菌毒素的筛查研究。结果显示，60%以上的样品检出1~4种真菌毒素，个别品种甚至检出10种以上。
这表明中药材的真菌毒素污染具有高度的复杂性，即一种中药材存在多种真菌毒素同时污染的情况，
且不同的中药材产生的真菌毒素污染各不相同。因此，建立中药材中真菌毒素的高通量检测方法对于
进一步完善中药的安全性质量控制标准和保障中药的食药用安全具有重要意义。
对于常见真菌毒素的检测，如AFs，通常采用免疫亲和柱净化-液相色谱-荧光检测器检测的方法，

chunks.text:
中药材中真菌毒素的高通量检测方法对于
进一步完善中药的安全性质量控制标准和保障中药的食药用安全具有重要意义。
对于常见真菌毒素的检测，如AFs，通常采用免疫亲和柱净化-液相色谱-荧光检测器检测的方法，
专属性好、灵敏度高。但由于中药材中复杂代谢物造成的严重基质干扰，加之同时适用多毒素的免疫
亲和柱难以获得，以及液相色谱-荧光检测法的光信号不稳定易受背景干扰等
［10］，使得该方法用于多
类别真菌毒素的高通量检测存在明显的局限性。相较于传统方法，液相色谱-质谱联用技术（LC-MS/
MS）具有更优的选择性和灵敏度，能够有效克服基质干扰，提高目标物定性和定量的准确性，已在复
杂基质的微痕量污染物分析中得到了广泛应用
［11］。目前，《中国药典》四部9305中药中真菌毒素测定指
导原则以及《上海市中药饮片炮制规范》分别收录了中药材中33种和62种真菌毒素的LC-MS/MS检测方
法
［12-13］，且均以QqQ 作为检测器。这表明同时监测多类别真菌毒素是中药材中真菌毒素污染检测研究
的一个重要趋势。
综上，本文从样品前处理、液相色谱分离以及液相色谱串联低分辨质谱和液相色谱串联高分辨质
谱检测等方面，对基于LC-MS/MS 的真菌毒素检测研究进行系统综述，并结合该技术目前在中药中的
应用情况，为基于LC-MS/MS的中药材中真菌毒素的检测方法研究和开发提供参考。

液相色谱串联高分辨质
谱检测等方面，对基于LC-MS/MS 的真菌毒素检测研究进行系统综述，并结合该技术目前在中药中的
应用情况，为基于LC-MS/MS的中药材中真菌毒素的检测方法研究和开发提供参考。
1 基于LC-MS/MS的样品前处理技术
在真菌毒素的检测分析中，样品前处理技术是确保分析结果的可靠、准确的关键步骤。其核心在
于高效提取目标分析物的同时，最大程度地去除中药复杂基质干扰成分，以克服严重的离子抑制效应。
针对中药高糖、高脂、高色素及代谢物复杂的特性，研究者们开发出多种样品前处理技术，包括固相
萃取法、改良QuEChERS法、稀释-直接进样法和磁固相萃取法等
［14-16］。

集效率高、回收率好，已成为真菌毒素检测常用的样品前处理技术之一
［17］。SPE法的核心在于吸附剂，
常见的吸附剂如下：（1）适用于吸附非极性或弱极性成分的反相吸附剂，如C18和C8等；（2）适用于吸附
极性成分的正相吸附剂，如CN、NH2和Florisil 等；（3）适用于吸附或去除离子类成分的离子交换吸附
剂，如强阴离子交换柱（SAX）、丙基磺酸柱（PRS）和乙二胺-N-丙基硅烷（PSA）等；（4）混合模式吸附
剂，如HLB 等
［18］。在方法开发过程中，可根据待测物和基质成分的理化性质差异对SPE 柱的吸附剂进
行选择，并优化洗脱溶剂和洗脱程序等，使方法获得优异的选择性。
在基于LC-MS 的真菌毒素检测中，前处理常用的SPE 柱主要有HLB 柱、Florisil 柱等。Bai 等
［19］在
当归中农药和真菌毒素的检测中，系统比较了HLB 柱和Carb/NH2柱的净化效果。结果表明，HLB 填料
凭借其独特的亲水-亲脂平衡特性，不仅能高效吸附不同极性的真菌毒素，包括AFs、OTA、ZEN、T-2，

chunks.text:
药和真菌毒素的检测中，系统比较了HLB 柱和Carb/NH2柱的净化效果。结果表明，HLB 填料
凭借其独特的亲水-亲脂平衡特性，不仅能高效吸附不同极性的真菌毒素，包括AFs、OTA、ZEN、T-2，
还能通过适度的亲脂作用选择性去除当归中的弱极性干扰成分，获得最优的定量性能，即平均回收率
为88. 96%，相对标准偏差（RSD）为8. 14%。但由于HLB 聚合物基质的吸附位点有限，其对某些极端极
性（强极性或弱极性）的真菌毒素吸附能力不足。相比之下，Florisil 柱在保留强极性化合物方面更具优
势。Zhang 等
［20］的研究证实，利用Florisil 柱表面硅醇基团与平面分子结构的特异性相互作用，可使李
子中DON 的回收率达97%。传统的SPE 材料在实际真菌毒素的检测应用中也存在一些不足，例如，
HLB 柱广谱性强但选择性较低；Florisil 柱对极性化合物的吸附过强且不可逆。近年来，新型的功能化
吸附材料不断涌现。郭大凯等
［21］开发的MIL-101（Cr）金属有机框架材料，因其独特的介孔分子筛结构、
超高比表面积和丰富的Cr3+不饱和配位位点，在玉米和小麦基质中展现出优异的真菌毒素吸附性能。
该材料不仅能同时覆盖9种不同结构的真菌毒素（回收率达83. 5%~116. 6%），还兼具选择性识别和高效

超高比表面积和丰富的Cr3+不饱和配位位点，在玉米和小麦基质中展现出优异的真菌毒素吸附性能。
该材料不仅能同时覆盖9种不同结构的真菌毒素（回收率达83. 5%~116. 6%），还兼具选择性识别和高效
富集的双重优势。其介孔结构可通过尺寸筛分效应实现选择性吸附，而Cr3+活性位点则通过与毒素分
子中特定官能团的配位作用增强吸附特异性，从而显著提高了复杂基质中痕量真菌毒素的富集效率。
也有研究团队成功制备了氨基和羟基双功能化的磁性微孔有机网络（Fe3O4@MON-NH2-OH）
［22］，该材料
通过氢键、疏水和π-π 叠加的协同作用，对中药样品中痕量ZEN 展现出215. 0 mg/g 的超高吸附容量，
定量下限达1. 4~3. 5 μg/kg。新型材料的涌现为SPE 技术注入了新的发展活力，但目前多数仍处于实验
室自制阶段，要实现商品化推广和广泛应用仍需进一步研究和优化。
1. 2　改良QuEChERS法
QuEChERS 法在2003 年被Anastassiades 等
［23］首次用于从蔬菜和水果中提取农药残留，其流程包括
提取和净化2个部分，提取溶剂采用乙腈，净化采用分散固相萃取（d-SPE）。随着该方法在不同基质中
的推广应用，通过提取溶剂、盐析及净化填料等的优化而建立的改良QuEChERS 法，由于其快速、简

chunks.text:
包括
提取和净化2个部分，提取溶剂采用乙腈，净化采用分散固相萃取（d-SPE）。随着该方法在不同基质中
的推广应用，通过提取溶剂、盐析及净化填料等的优化而建立的改良QuEChERS 法，由于其快速、简
单、廉价、有效、耐用和安全的优点，常被用作中药材中真菌毒素检测的首选样品前处理方法
［24］。
近年来，QuEChERS 法的提取溶剂由单一的乙腈向多样化、复合溶剂发展。常用的提取溶剂有甲
醇、乙腈、丙酮等，常用的提取方法有超声法、匀浆法、振荡法等。通常依据目标真菌毒素的极性选
择合适的提取溶剂
［25］。Xing等
［26］在研究枸杞中ATs的检测方法时，发现采用添加1. 5%甲酸的乙腈溶液
作为提取溶剂时，不仅能有效降低共提取物干扰，还可显著提高ATs的提取效率，使回收率达到74%~
105%。这一结果进一步验证了酸性改良剂在极性真菌毒素提取中的重要作用。针对中药这一复杂的基
质体系，研究者们进一步优化了混合溶剂提取方案，如Huang 等
［27］在检测莲子、薏苡仁等4 种典型中
药材中73种真菌毒素时，采用乙腈-水-乙酸（80∶19∶1）三元溶剂系统，成功实现了61. 6%~118. 6%的
宽谱系回收率，不仅证实了混合溶剂在中药多种毒素检测中的普适性优势，也为建立中药真菌毒素检
测标准方法提供了重要的技术参考。

chunks.text:
乙酸（80∶19∶1）三元溶剂系统，成功实现了61. 6%~118. 6%的
宽谱系回收率，不仅证实了混合溶剂在中药多种毒素检测中的普适性优势，也为建立中药真菌毒素检
测标准方法提供了重要的技术参考。
基于d-SPE 的净化是改良QuEChERS 法的另一重要步骤，中性氧化铝、C18、石墨化碳黑（GCB）和
PSA等是常用的净化填料。Zhao等
［28］系统评估了C18、PSA、-NH2、MCX和GCB五种吸附剂对肉豆蔻中
6 种链格孢毒素的净化性能，研究表明，C18凭借其适度的疏水相互作用，不仅能高效去除脂溶性干扰
物，还避免了PSA 和-NH2因与基质中酚类化合物竞争结合位点而导致含羟基的目标毒素共吸附的问
题。同时，相较于GCB 因π-π 堆积引起的毒素不可逆吸附，以及MCX 依赖的离子交换机制可能造成
的目标毒素损失，C18展现出更优异的综合净化性能，6种链格孢毒素的回收率在76%~104%之间。这一

发现为含高脂类成分的中药中真菌毒素的检测提供了可靠的净化方案。然而，随着分析要求的提高，
C18的非特异性疏水作用机制逐渐显现出局限性，尤其在处理含大量色素的复杂基质，以及多环芳烃或
极性杂原子化合物时净化效果欠佳。针对这一技术瓶颈，新型功能化吸附材料的开发为复杂基质分析

chunks.text:
分析要求的提高，
C18的非特异性疏水作用机制逐渐显现出局限性，尤其在处理含大量色素的复杂基质，以及多环芳烃或
极性杂原子化合物时净化效果欠佳。针对这一技术瓶颈，新型功能化吸附材料的开发为复杂基质分析
提供了突破性解决方案。其中，ENVI-Carb吸附剂通过其独特的石墨化表面结构和π-π电子相互作用，
可特异性吸附平面芳香化合物。Zhou 等
［29］对辣椒中AFs、OTA 等12种真菌毒素的检测研究表明，该材
料在高效去除色素的同时，仍能保持77. 3%~109. 2% 的优异回收率，而C18作为吸附剂时的回收率仅为
30%~50%。此外，多壁碳纳米管（MWCNTs）因特殊的中空管状结构和超高比表面积，不仅显著提升了
对极性化合物的吸附容量，还通过独特的尺寸排阻效应有效规避了大分子干扰。彭晓俊等
［30］的研究证
实，改性MWCNTs凭借其结构优势可高效去除新会陈皮中的黄酮类化合物（吸附率>90%），在新会陈皮
AFs、ZEN 等9 种真菌毒素检测中的回收率达72. 4%~106%，显著优于传统PSA、硅胶等吸附剂。
QuEChERS 法作为一种集提取与净化功能于一体的样品前处理技术，能够实现多种真菌毒素的同步提

分析各类真菌毒素，无需衍生化处理；其广泛的适用性也可满足各类真菌毒素的检测需求；与质谱联
用后，更可实现复杂基质中多种真菌毒素的高效同步检测和准确定量。这些特性使LC-MS/MS 技术成
为当前真菌毒素分析的首选方法
［40］，为安全监测提供了更为可靠和高效的解决方案。
近年来，液相色谱分离技术发展迅速，特别是耐高压系统和亚-2 μm/亚-3 μm 粒径填料的出现，
进一步提升了液相色谱分离复杂基质的性能
［41］。这些技术发展优化了传质动力学，减少了溶剂使用量，
增强了色谱分离度和分离效率，使超高效液相色谱-串联质谱技术（UPLC-MS/MS）成为检测中药复杂基
质中微痕量污染物的重要手段
［42］。例如，张成

［42］。例如，张成

该技术通过整合两种独立且正交的分离机制

综上，基于低分辨质谱的LC-MS/MS 在真菌毒素高通量检测中表现出优越的灵敏度和选择性，是
目前中药真菌毒素定性、定量的主要方法。然而，该方法在真菌毒素的大规模筛查应用中仍存在以下
局限性：（1）高度依赖高纯度标准品，需通过标准品优化各毒素的定性/定量离子对及碰撞能量等关键
质谱参数，而部分隐蔽型真菌毒素标准品难以获取；（2）作为一种靶向检测技术，仅能监测预设列表中

5 结语与展望
真菌毒素在中药中的污染风险及其对人体健康的潜在危害不容忽视，因此建立高效、可靠的检测
方法具有重要的科学意义和应用价值。中药基质的高度复杂性是开发高通量检测技术的核心挑战。一
方面，中药含有丰富的初级和次级代谢产物，且不同药材的代谢成分差异显著，导致基质干扰类型多
样、程度不一；另一方面，药材的理化特性使样品前处理和仪器分析面临极大困难。这些由药材种类
决定的基质差异，使得基于LC-MS/MS 的高通量分析必须兼顾高灵敏度和高抗干扰能力，以确保痕量
真菌毒素的准确测定。
目前，针对中药基质的特点，前处理多依赖SPE、QuEChERS 及稀释-直接进样等技术。然而，我

在检测平台选择上，QqQ 质谱（包括QTrap）凭借其卓越的灵敏度、稳定性和成熟的定量能力，目

力构建和完善适用于中药基质的高分辨质谱分析流程，提升其定量稳健性与数据处理效率，并加强其
与高灵敏QqQ 平台的技术融合与数据互证，构建“靶向定量+非靶向筛查”的双重保障体系。最终目
标在于建立覆盖广泛药材类型、通量高、抗干扰能力强、结果准确可靠的真菌毒素检测技术网络，为
中药从源头到产品的全程质量安全构筑更为坚实的技术防线。

【中文摘要】Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy via JNK, ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling in human lung carcinoma cells
标题：桑根酮（Morusin）通过JNK、ERK和PI3K/Akt信号通路诱导人肺癌细胞凋亡和自噬
关键词：桑根酮，桑白皮，桑（Morus alba），肺癌，非小细胞肺癌，A549细胞，NCI-H292细胞，凋亡，自噬，增殖抑制，线粒体膜电位，JNK通路，ERK通路，PI3K/Akt通路，LY294002，SP600125，U0126
摘要：本研究从桑白皮（桑Morus alba根皮）中提取的天然异戊烯基黄酮类化合物桑根酮（Morusin），探讨其对非小细胞肺癌A549和NCI-H292细胞的抗癌作用。结果显示，桑根酮通过抑制PI3K/Akt信号、激活JNK和ERK通路，诱导线粒体依赖性凋亡（染色质凝聚、PARP切割、MMP丢失、细胞色素c释放、Bax/Bcl-2失调、caspase-3激活）和自噬（LC3-II升高、SQSTM1/p62降低），从而抑制细胞增殖。

sistance and side effects, the development of novel therapeutics for the treatment of lung cancer is
still in an urgent need. Morusin, a naturally occurring prenylated flavonoid isolated from the root bark of Morus
alba, has been reported to be a promising candidate for cancer treatment including lung cancer. This study aimed
to validate the anti-cancer effects of morusin in human non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cell lines A549 and
NCI–H292. The results indicated that morusin had growth inhibitory, pro-apoptotic and pro-autophagic effects
chunks.title: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy via JNK, ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling in human lung carcinoma cells

chunks.text:
. The results indicated that morusin had growth inhibitory, pro-apoptotic and pro-autophagic effects
on A549 and NCI–H292 cells. The induction of apoptosis was characterized by chromatin condensation and
PARP cleavage. Mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) loss, cytochrome c release, Bax/Bcl-2 dysregulation,
and caspase-3 cleavage were also observed, indicating a mitochondria-dependent apoptosis was induced by
morusin. A pro-autophagic effect was demonstrated by the increased level of LC3-II and decreased level of
chunks.title: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy via JNK, ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling in human lung carcinoma cells
chunks.filename: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy.pdf

chunks.text:
in. A pro-autophagic effect was demonstrated by the increased level of LC3-II and decreased level of
SQSTM1/p62. Furthermore, morusin inhibited PI3K/Akt signaling and activated JNK, ERK pathways as indi­
cated by the alteration in the ratio of phosphorylation level over total protein expression level. A PI3K/Akt
inhibitor (LY294002), a JNK inhibitor (SP600125) and a MEK/ERK inhibitor (U0126) contributed to the
determination that these pathways were involved in both apoptosis and autophagy induced by morusin.

1. Introduction
Cancer has been a major public health problem worldwide for many
years. Lung cancer is considered as the most common type of cancer and
by far the leading cause of cancer-related deaths in the world. According
to cancer statistics released by the American Cancer Society, approxi­

chunks.text:
eaths in the world. According
to cancer statistics released by the American Cancer Society, approxi­
mately 228,820 new lung cancer cases and 135,720 lung cancer deaths
were projected to occur in the United States in 2020. The 5-year relative
survival rate for lung cancer is only 19%, which is among the lowest of
all cancer types [1]. Treatment options for lung cancer include surgery,
chemotherapy, radiation therapy, immunotherapy and targeted ther­
apy. Despite the improvements in therapeutics especially novel
molecular-targeted approaches emerged during the past decades, the

chunks.text:
in therapeutics especially novel
molecular-targeted approaches emerged during the past decades, the
death rate of lung cancer remains the highest among all cancer types [2].
Therefore, development of novel therapies is still in an urgent need.
Natural products have been demonstrated as the most prolific source
of lead compounds for the development of anti-cancer drugs [3].
Prenylated flavonoids represented a subgroup of natural occurring fla­
vonoids possessing at least one C5 isoprene unit in their structure. The
introduction of lipophilic prenyl side chain(s) into flavonoid skeleton
chunks.title: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy via JNK, ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling in human lung carcinoma cells

chunks.text:
unit in their structure. The
introduction of lipophilic prenyl side chain(s) into flavonoid skeleton
might enhance interactions between flavonoids and the phospholipid
membranes or hydrophobic target proteins, consequently increase the
bioactivities of flavonoids [4]. Increasing evidences suggested that
prenylation was a determinant factor for the enhancement of cytotox­
icity of flavonoid, this made prenylated flavonoids as attractive com­
pounds for obtaining anti-cancer leading structures [5]. The root bark of
Morus alba (mulberry tree), named as Sangbaipi in Chinese, was
chunks.title: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy via JNK, ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling in human lung carcinoma cells

ding structures [5]. The root bark of
Morus alba (mulberry tree), named as Sangbaipi in Chinese, was
demonstrated to be a good resource of prenylated flavonoids. During our
exploration of cytotoxic prenylated flavonoids, we performed a bioassay
guided isolation of Sangbaipi, morusin was obtained together with many
other compounds [6]. Among the obtained compounds, morusin was the
most effective and abundant one. It has been reported that morusin
could induce the apoptosis of colorectal [7], lung [8], breast [9], pros­
tate [10], gastric [11] and hepatoma [12] cancer cells. The mechanism

could induce paraptosis-like cell death in epithelial ovarian cancer cells
[13]. In this study, the effects of morusin on cell growth in two human
lung cancer cell lines, A549 and NCI–H292, were explored. The results

transmit extracellular signals into cells [14,15]. These two pathways
also regulate or have crosstalk with other important signaling such as
NF-κB and STAT3 [16], through these intracellular signaling, cell sur­
vival and death are regulated [17]. In this study, the regulation of MAPK
and PI3K/Akt pathways by morusin in A549 and NCI–H292 cells were

4. Discussion
As the leading cause of cancer mortality worldwide, lung cancer
contributed one-quarter of all cancer deaths. Although there has been a
steady increase in survival for most cancer types since the mid-1970s,
advances have been slow for lung cancer [33]. Recent years, targeted
agents such as EGFR inhibitors showed promising effects in the treat­
chunks.title: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy via JNK, ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling in human lung carcinoma cells
chunks.filename: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy.pdf

chunks.text:
r [33]. Recent years, targeted
agents such as EGFR inhibitors showed promising effects in the treat­
ment of advanced non-small-cell lung cancer, but this was mainly
limited for cancers with EGFR mutation [34]. For most types of lung
cancers, developing new therapeutics that can serve as alternative
strategic options is still in an urgent need. Morusin is a prenylated
flavonoid obtained from the root bark of Morus alba. According to pre­
vious reports, morusin possessed anti-cancer activities against several
kinds of cancer cells [10,11,13]. In this study, we demonstrated that
chunks.title: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy via JNK, ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling in human lung carcinoma cells
chunks.filename: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy.pdf

chunks.text:
cer activities against several
kinds of cancer cells [10,11,13]. In this study, we demonstrated that
morusin activated both apoptosis and autophagy in two kinds of
non-small-cell lung cancer cells, A549 and NCI–H292.
Apoptosis is a programmed cellular process that occurs under either
physiological or pathological conditions. Induction of cancer cell
apoptosis is the eventual aim of many cancer therapies. Annexin V/PI
double staining and DAPI staining results indicated that morusin
induced apoptosis in the two cell lines. The signaling pathways for
chunks.title: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy via JNK, ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling in human lung carcinoma cells
chunks.filename: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy.pdf

chunks.text:
g results indicated that morusin
induced apoptosis in the two cell lines. The signaling pathways for
apoptosis are divided into two distinct categories: intrinsic and extrinsic
pathways [35,36]. The intrinsic pathway is also called the mitochondrial
pathway due to the involvement of mitochondria. In this study, the
cleavage of caspase-9, loss of MMP, released cytochrome c into cytosol,
increased level of Bax and decreased level of Bcl-2 revealed that morusin
induced apoptosis was through intrinsic mitochondrial apoptotic
pathway.
Although apoptosis was induced by morusin treatment, we noticed
chunks.title: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy via JNK, ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling in human lung carcinoma cells
chunks.filename: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy.pdf

chunks.text:
sic mitochondrial apoptotic
pathway.
Although apoptosis was induced by morusin treatment, we noticed
that the apoptosis rate was lower than the cell death rate, this reminded
us there might be other cell death pathway except for apoptosis. Auto­
phagy is another mode of programmed cell death and usually acts before
apoptosis occurred when cells encounter outer membrane stresses. LC3-
II and SQSTM1 are representative markers of autophagy [26]. After
morusin treatment for half an hour, the protein levels of LC3-II and
SQSTM1 were detected to be regulated inversely, LC3-II increased and
chunks.title: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy via JNK, ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling in human lung carcinoma cells
chunks.filename: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy.pdf

chunks.text:
he protein levels of LC3-II and
SQSTM1 were detected to be regulated inversely, LC3-II increased and
SQSTM1 decreased, this suggested the occurring of autophagy (Fig. 3A).
To further verify the induction of autophagy, tandem RFP-GFP-LC3 was
transfected into cells, immunofluorescence images indicated the in­
duction of autophagic flux (Fig. 3B). Since autophagy can act both as a
cell survival and cell death process, we used an autophagy inhibitor
chloroquine to demonstrate that morusin-induced autophagy promoted
cell death (Fig. 4C).

chunks.filename: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy.pdf

chunks.text:
y inhibitor
chloroquine to demonstrate that morusin-induced autophagy promoted
cell death (Fig. 4C).
ERK and JNK, known as members of MAPK family, play a key role in
regulating cell growth, proliferation and cell survival [37]. PI3K-Akt
pathway also plays an important role in controlling cell survival and
death [38]. In this study, we examined the phosphorylation status of
ERK, JNK and Akt to elucidate the possible mechanisms that are
involved in morusin-induced apoptosis and autophagy. The results
showed that morusin phosphorylated ERK and JNK, but dephosphory­
chunks.title: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy via JNK, ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling in human lung carcinoma cells
chunks.filename: Morusin induces apoptosis and autophagy.pdf

chunks.text:
poptosis and autophagy. The results
showed that morusin phosphorylated ERK and JNK, but dephosphory­
lated Akt (Fig. 4A and B). As an Akt downstream target, NF-κB was
shown to be inhibited accordingly (Fig. 6A). The use of corresponding
inhibitors of each pathway revealed the involvement of ERK, JNK and
Akt pathways in morusin-induced apoptosis and autophagy (Fig. 4D and
E).
All of the pathways mentioned above are reported to be responsive to
multiple stress stimuli including oxidative stress [39]. In this study, ROS
generation was detected as increased significantly after morusin treat­

decreased cell viability through inducing endogenous apoptosis and

【中文摘要】Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs
标题：污染中药材中真菌和真菌毒素的发生与特征分析

关键词：中药材，真菌污染，真菌毒素，黄曲霉毒素，赭曲霉毒素A，桔霉素，党参（Codonopsis radix），黄芩（Scutellariae radix），高效液相色谱-串联质谱（HPLC-MS/MS），形态学鉴定，分子鉴定，曲霉属（Aspergillus spp.），青霉属（Penicillium spp.）

摘要：本研究评估了13种不同中药材共48份污染样品中的主要真菌菌群和真菌毒素污染程度。结果显示，70.8%的样品受到黄曲霉毒素轻微污染（<5 µg kg⁻¹），党参样品检出赭曲霉毒素A（360–515 µg kg⁻¹），黄芩样品检出赭曲霉毒素A（49–231 µg kg⁻¹）和桔霉素（15–53 µg kg⁻¹）。通过形态学和分子鉴定，共分离出69株真菌，主要菌属包括曲霉属（26.1%）、青霉属（24.6%）、根霉属（14.5%）和木霉属（11.6%），并采用高效液相色谱-串联质谱法在37株培养物中检测到黄曲霉毒素、赭曲霉毒素A和桔霉素。

fungi during cultivation, harvesting, and storage, causing spoilage and mycotoxin production.

in Codonopsis radix and Scutellariae radix, it alludes to the need to establish a maximum permitted
level for these medicinal herbs that are commonly consumed by humans.
1. Introduction
Chinese medicinal herbs are an invaluable asset to China, and widely used in medicinal, edible,

Chinese medicinal herbs are an invaluable asset to China, and widely used in medicinal, edible,
and health products. With the continuous development of traditional medicinal herbs, the eﬃcacy of

medicinal herbs is recognized and valued, and its safety is a subject of concern. There have been many
reports about the international trade obstacles of Chinese medicinal herbs in recent years, mainly on

chunks.text:
eports about the international trade obstacles of Chinese medicinal herbs in recent years, mainly on
the case of excessive levels of extrinsic harmful residues in medicinal herbs including mycotoxins,
pesticides, heavy metals, and sulfur dioxide [1–3].
Mildew is the primary cause of mycotoxin contamination among medicinal herbs. Medicinal herbs
have been produced primarily through the traditional open, small workshop, and scattered planting
business models. No uniform standard or eﬃcient supervision method has been reported for processing,
chunks.title: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs

chunks.text:
business models. No uniform standard or eﬃcient supervision method has been reported for processing,
storage, and transportation of medicinal herbs. Mismanagement of medicinal herbs during processing,
storage, and transportation and their intrinsic factors and external environmental conditions lead to
severe spoilage and deterioration, along with mycotoxigenic fungi contamination. The majority of
mycotoxin producers can be found in the fungal genera Aspergillus, Penicillium, Fusarium, and Alternaria
chunks.title: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs
chunks.filename: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs.pdf

chunks.text:
toxin producers can be found in the fungal genera Aspergillus, Penicillium, Fusarium, and Alternaria
which concomitantly happen to be the most abundant contaminants of food as well as medicinal herbs.
The medicinal herbs (e.g., Notoginseng radix et rhizoma, Scutellariae radix, Morindae oﬃcinalis radix)
are easily contaminated with molds producing mycotoxins such as ochratoxin A (OTA) [4]. Plant
seeds (e.g., Coicis semen) are rich in starch, protein, and fat, which are highly susceptible to fungal
contamination. The molds and mycotoxins contamination occur frequently in processing due to the

chunks.text:
ngal
contamination. The molds and mycotoxins contamination occur frequently in processing due to the
heavily rainy days in harvest season as well as inappropriate storage and transportation of Coicis
semen [5]. Mildew infestation in herbal medicines cause large-scale fungal growth and mycotoxin
accumulation, thus aﬀecting the quality and eﬃcacy of medicinal herbs. More than 400 types of
mycotoxins reportedly pose a risk to human health. Mycotoxins are secondary metabolites primarily
produced by diﬀerent fungal species. The mycotoxins contaminating medicinal herbs commonly
chunks.title: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs

chunks.text:
primarily
produced by diﬀerent fungal species. The mycotoxins contaminating medicinal herbs commonly
include aﬂatoxins (AFs), OTA, and citrinin (CTN) [6]. Recent studies have found that Chinese herbal
medicines can be simultaneously contaminated by various fungi, especially during storage [7]. The
synergistic side eﬀects of several mycotoxins on animal health and agricultural product performance
are greater than those of individual mycotoxins [8]. For example, when OTA is used alone, the mortality
chunks.title: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs
chunks.filename: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs.pdf

chunks.text:
greater than those of individual mycotoxins [8]. For example, when OTA is used alone, the mortality
rate is not high; however, it exerts synergistic eﬀects with aﬂatoxins to increase the harmful eﬀects of
aﬂatoxins [9].
China is a large-scale producer of medicinal plant resources, with large-scale utilization of
medicinal herbs [10]. Most medicinal herbs have a gradual and lasting eﬀect. Some diseases require
long-term use of medicinal herbs to achieve therapeutic outcomes. Certain medicinal herbs including
chunks.title: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs

chunks.text:
long-term use of medicinal herbs to achieve therapeutic outcomes. Certain medicinal herbs including
Coicis semen and Jujubae fructus, which are used in medicines and food items, have also long been
consumed as health foods. The long-term use of traditional medicinal herbs contaminated with
mycotoxins may increase the incidence of adverse reactions [11]. Owing to the limited information
available on toxigenic molds in medicinal herbs, this study aimed to evaluate the predominant mycoﬂora
and the extent of fungal contamination in 13 diﬀerent species of medicinal herbs (Jujubae fructus,

and the extent of fungal contamination in 13 diﬀerent species of medicinal herbs (Jujubae fructus,
Amomi fructus, Lycii fructus; Notoginseng radix et rhizoma, Codonopsis radix, Scutellariae radix, Morindae
oﬃcinalis radix, Polygoni multiﬂori radix; Coicis semen; Poria; Ganoderma lucidum, Tremella fuciformis,
Lentinus edodes) in common use from China, and to investigate their potential ability to produce
mycotoxins from isolated fungi, such as aﬂatoxin B1 (AFB1), aﬂatoxin B2 (AFB2), aﬂatoxin G1 (AFG1),
aﬂatoxin G2 (AFG2), CTN, and OTA.

2.1. Mycotoxin Detection
The high-performance liquid chromatography with ﬂuorescence detection (HPLC-FLD) method
(Figure S1) was optimized for the detection and quantiﬁcation of six mycotoxins in medicinal herbs. The
chromatogram, limit of quantiﬁcation (LOQ), and limit of detection (LOD) are summarized in Figure
S1 and Table S1. LOD values determined herein ranged from 0.012 µg kg−1 for AFB1 to 1.3 µg kg−1
for CTN. Among 48 medicinal herbs, 39 (81.3%) samples were positive for mycotoxins beyond their

AFG2, and OTA). In the case of medicinal plants, oﬃcial regulations regarding the presence of only
aﬂatoxins and OTA in medicinal herbs are shared globally among pharmacopoeias and national and

organizational regulations. In general, the current legal limit for AFB1 in medicinal herbs ranges
between 2 µg kg−1 and 10 µg kg−1, while the limit for total aﬂatoxins (combined AFB1, AFB2, AFG1,
and AFG2) ranges from 4 µg kg−1 to 20 µg kg−1, and the limit for OTA rangs from 15 µg kg−1 to 80 µg
kg−1 [10]. Herein, 70.8% (34/48) of medicinal herbs were contaminated with AFB1; however their
levels were within the permissible limits (5 µg kg−1). AFB1 and OTA were simultaneously detected in

concentrations were higher than 1.2–158.7 µg kg−1 reported previously for 23 OTA-contaminated
mold samples by Yang et al. [12]. OTA has been classiﬁed by the International Agency for Research
on Cancer (IARC) as a potential carcinogen (group 2B) on the basis of suﬃcient animal studies [13].
The recommended provisional tolerable weekly intakes (PTWI) for OTA is 100 ng kg−1 body weight

has reported a tolerable daily intake (TDI) of 5 ng kg−1 bw [15].

2.2. Fungal Contamination
The association between fungal species and medicinal herbs remains unclear owing to
complex sources of contamination including extrinsic (environmental and geographical) and intrinsic
(constituents of each herbal species) factors [16]. Owing to the widespread presence of fungi in nature,
medicinal herbs are often susceptible to fungal contamination inadequately treated during production
chunks.title: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs
chunks.filename: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs.pdf

chunks.text:
medicinal herbs are often susceptible to fungal contamination inadequately treated during production
and storage. The presence of fungi in 48 sample of 13 diﬀerent medicinal herbs (each ≥3 batches) were
detected, results showed that 83.3% (40/48) were positive for fungi, demonstrating the majority of
Chinese medicinal herbs were contaminated with fungi.
Sixty-nine fungi (64 strains of mold and 5 strains of yeast) were isolated from 48 medicinal herb
samples. Preliminary morphological identiﬁcation revealed 18 strains of Aspergillus, 17 strains of
chunks.title: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs

chunks.text:
b
samples. Preliminary morphological identiﬁcation revealed 18 strains of Aspergillus, 17 strains of
Penicillium, 10 strains of Rhizopus, 8 strains of Trichoderma, 4 strains of Mucor, 5 strains of yeast, 2 strains
of Byssochlamys, 2 strains of Chaetomium, 1 strain of Alternaria, 1 strain of Mycosis, and 1 strain of
Neurospora. The colony morphology of the primary strains are shown in Figure 1. Traditionally, fungi in
medicinal herbs have been divided into two distinct classes: ﬁeld fungi (e.g., Fusarium, Alternaria),
chunks.title: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs
chunks.filename: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs.pdf

chunks.text:
edicinal herbs have been divided into two distinct classes: ﬁeld fungi (e.g., Fusarium, Alternaria),
which invade and produce their toxins before harvest; and storage fungi (e.g., Aspergillus, Penicillium),
which become a problem after harvest [17]. Moreover, some fungi (e.g., Aspergillus) might belong to
both classes before and after harvest. The predominant mycoﬂora isolated in this study were storage
fungi. Particularly the primary isolated strains from Codonopsis radix and Scutellariae radix were
Penicillium polonicum, which potentially produce CTN.

Mildewed medicinal herbs were markedly contaminated with fungi.
Overall, Aspergillus
and Penicillium were the most frequent contaminants, concurrent with previous ﬁndings [18,19].
Reproduction in Aspergillus spp.
requires a substrate with a higher water activity, suggesting
that the medicinal herbs herein may be not dried in time after harvesting, or that drying was
gradual and the duration of dehydration was too long, resulting in subsequent mold propagation.

gradual and the duration of dehydration was too long, resulting in subsequent mold propagation.
The present drying procedure should be strengthened to reduce the possibility of mold contamination.
Furthermore, herbal medicines are often aﬀected with mildew during storage owing to poor
management, especially in southern China. Currently, various methods can be used to reduce fungal

prevention of fungal growth at the source to reduce in contaminated medicinal herbs. Special measures
against mildew are required to establish a scientiﬁc and reasonable monitoring system, from the
beginning of harvesting at the site of origin, with particular attention to the control of mold pollution,

(Figure S1). Mycotoxins were detected positive in eight strains (Figure 2), e.g., AFB1 and AFB2 were
simultaneously detected in one strain of Aspergillus ﬂavus (from Amomi fructus 08-3), CTN was detected

3. Conclusions
This study systematically investigated the prevalence of fungi and mycotoxins in medicinal herbs.
A relatively large number of medicinal herbs were found to be contaminated, mainly by Aspergillus
and Penicillium. OTA was detected at high levels in Codonopsis radix and Scutellariae radix. CTN was
chunks.title: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs
chunks.filename: Occurrence and Characterization of Fungi and Mycotoxins in Contaminated Medicinal Herbs.pdf

chunks.text:
and Penicillium. OTA was detected at high levels in Codonopsis radix and Scutellariae radix. CTN was
detected in Scutellariae radix at 53 µg kg−1. Subsequent analysis indicates that Penicillium polonicum
was the potential contributors to the high levels of CTN contamination in Scutellariae radix. Three
strains of Penicillium citrinum isolated from Ganoderma lucidum can produce CTN. The presence of
myco-fungi implies the potential for mycotoxin contamination under suitable conditions, and once the
mycotoxins is formed or exceeds the standard, thus could pose a potential health risk to consumers.

mycotoxins is formed or exceeds the standard, thus could pose a potential health risk to consumers.
Considering the toxicological eﬀects of OTA and CTN, a maximum permitted level in several medicinal
herbs is needed. Furthermore, these data may help to identify the species of medicinal herbs that
are more commonly associated with fungi and mycotoxin contaminations, and to provide useful
information for eﬀective prevent, control, and degrade contaminants strategies to ensure the safety of
medicinal herbs.

【中文摘要】Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
标题：国内中药材中真菌毒素（霉菌毒素）的发生与分析

关键词：中药材，真菌毒素，霉菌毒素，污染，分析，检测，高效液相色谱-串联质谱，LC-MS/MS，食品安全，质量控制

摘要：本研究调查了国内中药材中真菌毒素（霉菌毒素）的污染情况，采用高效液相色谱-串联质谱（LC-MS/MS）方法对多种中药材样品进行分析。结果显示，部分中药材受到黄曲霉毒素、赭曲霉毒素等真菌毒素的污染，提示需加强中药材在采收、加工和储存过程中的质量控制，以确保用药安全。

ABSTRACT
For time immemorial, Chinese herbal medicines (CHMs) have been widely used in China for disease
treatment and promotion of general well-being. However, in recent years, many studies have
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
r disease
treatment and promotion of general well-being. However, in recent years, many studies have
shown that mycotoxins produced by fungi could contaminate CHMs due to unfavourable pre- or
post-harvest conditions, raising major concern for consumer safety. At present, there is a signiﬁcant
focus on developing novel mycotoxin detection methods for analysing CHMs, and numerous
studies have aimed to determine which kinds of raw herbal materials are most susceptible to
mycotoxin contamination. In this review, we focus on recent advances in understanding and
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
eptible to
mycotoxin contamination. In this review, we focus on recent advances in understanding and
detection of mycotoxins in domestic raw herbal materials and related products from 2000 to
2018. Aspects of mycotoxin contamination of CHMs covered in this review include common
mycotoxin contaminants in CHMs, maximum mycotoxin residue limits, analytical methods for
mycotoxin detection and their applications and limitations, as well as a brief discussion of the
trends in ongoing research.

1. Introduction
Mycotoxins are secondary metabolites produced by
fungi during growth that can cause pathological
responses in humans and animals. Medicinal herbs
are highly susceptible to toxigenic fungal infections
and mycotoxin contamination that can occur at either
the pre- or post-harvest stage as a result of poor
growing conditions, inadequate drying, or storage in
warm, humid conditions (Zhang et al. 2016). The
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
growing conditions, inadequate drying, or storage in
warm, humid conditions (Zhang et al. 2016). The
potential for medicinal herbs and related agricultural
products to have toxic eﬀects as a result of mycotoxin
contamination
is
attracting
increasing
attention
worldwide (Tripathy et al. 2015; Mahfuz et al. 2018;
Zhang et al. 2018c). At present, the most common
mycotoxins
found
in
Chinese
herbal
medicines
(CHMs)
are
aﬂatoxins,
ochratoxins,
zearalenone,
fumonisins, trichothecenes, and patulin (Zhang et al.
2015). Numerous studies have shown that these
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
fumonisins, trichothecenes, and patulin (Zhang et al.
2015). Numerous studies have shown that these
mycotoxins are highly toxic resulting in hepatotoxi-
city,
nephrotoxicity,
reproductive
disorders,
and
immuno-suppression. These mycotoxins are also car-
cinogenic, teratogenic, and mutagenic making expo-
sure to compounds of this nature a serious human
health threat.
2. Aﬂatoxins (AFs)
In 1960, 100,000 turkeys died abruptly over the span
of a few months in the UK. People later found that
they had all consumed the same peanut meal that
was contaminated by fungi. As a result of this occur-
rence,
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
all consumed the same peanut meal that
was contaminated by fungi. As a result of this occur-
rence,
AFs
were
discovered
and
characterised
(Wannop 1961). AFs are secondary metabolites that
share a common difurocoumarin skeleton; they are
produced by Aspergillus ﬂavus and A. parasiticus (Shen
et al. 2016). This class of compounds includes aﬂa-
toxin B1, B2, G1, G2, M1, and M2; of these, AFB1 is the
most toxic and carcinogenic one. According to pre-
vious studies, the toxicity of AFB1 is 10 times greater
than that of cyanide and 68 times greater than that of
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
ies, the toxicity of AFB1 is 10 times greater
than that of cyanide and 68 times greater than that of
arsenic. In 1993, AFB1 was classiﬁed as a Class 1A
carcinogen by the World Health Organisation Cancer
Research Institute (Ono et al. 2001). Studies have
shown that AFB1 can suppress the immune system
and aﬀect foetal development and diﬀerentiation of
cells, giving this compound the ability to exert terato-
genic eﬀects. Exposure to AFB1 is also known to have
damaging eﬀects on human and animal liver tissues.
In severe cases, exposure to AFB1 resulted in liver
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
maging eﬀects on human and animal liver tissues.
In severe cases, exposure to AFB1 resulted in liver
cancer and even death (Ma and Zan 2009).

2.1. The limit standards of AFs
By the end of 2003, approximately 100 countries had
imposed speciﬁc limits on the levels of mycotoxins
allowed in food and feed (Food and Agriculture
Organization of the United Nations 2004). As depicted
in Table 1, in the case of medicinal herbs and related
products, the legal limit for AFB1 ranges from 2 to
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
le 1, in the case of medicinal herbs and related
products, the legal limit for AFB1 ranges from 2 to
10 μg∙kg−1, while the limit for other AFs ranges from 4
to 20 μg∙kg−1. Among these regulations, the European
Pharmacopeia (European Pharmacopoeia Commission
2016)
and
the
British
Pharmacopeia
(British
Pharmacopoeia Commission 2012) have set the strictest
limits (2 μg∙kg−1 for AFB1 and 4 μg∙kg−1 for total AFs), and
the most commonly set limits for AFB1 and AFs are
similar to those of the Chinese Pharmacopeia (Chinese
Pharmacopoeia Commission 2015) and the European
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
imilar to those of the Chinese Pharmacopeia (Chinese
Pharmacopoeia Commission 2015) and the European
Union (European Union 2006), which were 5 μg∙kg−1
and 10 μg∙kg−1, respectively.
2.2. Detection methods for AFs
Thin-layer chromatography (TLC) was the ﬁrst method
used for detecting AFs. In correlation with the increasing
demand for more precise data, the overall percentage of
use of TLC for detecting AFs was reduced. However, since
TLC is a straightforward approach with low-associated
cost and minimal specialised equipment, it is still gener-
ally utilised in some laboratories (Li et al. 2005).
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
nimal specialised equipment, it is still gener-
ally utilised in some laboratories (Li et al. 2005).
In recent years, high-performance liquid chromatogra-
phy (HPLC) has become the most common method for
quantifying AFs. Currently, HPLC with an FLD detector
(HPLC-FLD) is the most commonly used method for
detecting the presence of AFs and quantifying their
levels. However, aqueous solvents are often used as the
eluent in reverse-phase chromatography, and aqueous
buﬀers will partially quench the ﬂuorescence of AFB1 and
AFG1. Therefore, a derivatisation step is usually required
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
tially quench the ﬂuorescence of AFB1 and
AFG1. Therefore, a derivatisation step is usually required
to stabilise and enhance detection, such as a pre-column
derivatisation with triﬂuoroacetic acid (TFA) (Zhao et al.
2011; Li et al.2015) or a post-column derivatisation such
as a chemical derivatisation with iodine or bromine (Ran
et al. 2017), a photochemical derivatisation, or an electro-
chemical derivatisation (Zhang et al. 2005a; Zhang and
Chen 2005). Compared to pre-column derivatisations,
application of post-column derivatisations was reported
more frequently (Zhang et al. 2018c).
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
tions,
application of post-column derivatisations was reported
more frequently (Zhang et al. 2018c).
HPLC-MS/MS has been increasingly used for the
detection and quantiﬁcation of AFs in herbal medi-
cines (Wang et al. 2011; Liu et al. 2012; Saha et al.
2018). At the same time, HPLC-MS/MS is often used
for conﬁrmation of AF identity in order to avoid inter-
fering signals from analogs of AFs that might be pre-
sent in herbal medicines.
In addition to conventional analysis methods, immu-
nological methods have been used for rapid detection
of AFs in CHMs such as an enzyme-linked immunosor-
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
ogical methods have been used for rapid detection
of AFs in CHMs such as an enzyme-linked immunosor-
bent assay (ELISA) and a gold immunochromato-
graphic assay (GICA). Chu et al. (Chu et al. 2015) used
these approaches to successfully detect AFB1 in lotus
seeds. Since the complexity matrices presented by
CHMs can aﬀect the antigen-antibody speciﬁc binding
reaction, a matrix-matching curve was used to reduce
the bias introduced by the matrix. For example, using
AFB1-BSA and a sheep anti-mouse IgG antibody for
detection and a control, respectively, Yang generated
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
B1-BSA and a sheep anti-mouse IgG antibody for
detection and a control, respectively, Yang generated
a test strip suitable for rapid detection of AFB1 in lotus
seeds with a sensitivity of 2.5 ng∙mL−1 (Yang 2015).
Fluorescent immunoassays (FIAs) have recently been
developed for qualitative and quantitative analysis of AFs
in herbal matrices. Zhang established a ﬂuorescence
polarisation immunoassay detection method by comb-
ing AFB1 with amino ﬂuorescein. The molecular weight
and rotation speed of the AFB1 ﬂuorescent probe will
change before and after binding with an antibody. Thus,
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
tion speed of the AFB1 ﬂuorescent probe will
change before and after binding with an antibody. Thus,
detection and quantiﬁcation of AFB1 in CHMs can be
accomplished by measuring the change in the ﬂuores-
cence polarisation value (Zhang 2017). Based on the
development of a FITC-AFB1 ﬂuorescently labelled anti-
body, Yu et al. established a direct competitive ﬂuores-
cent immunoassay to detect AFB1 in ﬁve CHMs (Yu
et al.2015). Zhang utilised PEG-modiﬁed CdSe/CdS quan-
tum dots (QDs) with glycine-based signal enhancement
for the detection of AFB1 in medicinal herbs (Zhang et al.
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
Ds) with glycine-based signal enhancement
for the detection of AFB1 in medicinal herbs (Zhang et al.
2018b). This work demonstrated that a QD labelling
technique could potentially serve as a novel means of
performing fast trace-detection in complex herbal
matrices. Due to the AFB1 self-sensitisation to ﬂuores-
cence when under UV light, a label-free FIA method
was developed for the speciﬁc detection of AFB1 in
CHMs.
Compared
with
traditional
immunoassay
approaches, this method could reduce the cost of analy-
sis and shorten the analysis time without a complex
probe labelling process (Shu 2018).
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
st of analy-
sis and shorten the analysis time without a complex
probe labelling process (Shu 2018).

Ochratoxin A, ochratoxin B, ochratoxin C, and ochra-
toxin D are the main varieties of ochratoxins (Li and Ji
2003). Among the families of ochratoxin that have
been discovered, ochratoxin A (OTA) is considered to
be second after AFs in terms of prevalence and poten-
tial health hazards. OTA is carcinogenic, teratogenic,
neurotoxic, and exposure can also result in hepatotoxi-
city and nephrotoxicity. Therefore, OTA is a mycotoxin
and is classiﬁed as a Class IIB carcinogen by the
International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC)
(Shu et al. 2008).

3.1. Regulatory guidelines for OTA levels
In the case of medicinal plants, the EU has oﬃcial reg-
ulations on the level of OTA allowed in nutmeg, ginger,
turmeric, black and white pepper, and liquorice root and
its extract, with the legal limit varying from 15 μg∙kg−1 to
80 μg∙kg−1 (European Union 2006). In Vietnam, the limit
for OTA levels ranges from 20 μg∙kg−1 to 80 μg∙kg−1
(United States Department of Agriculture Foreign
Agricultural Service 2013) (Table 3).
3.2. Detection methods for OTA

Agricultural Service 2013) (Table 3).
3.2. Detection methods for OTA
As described in previous studies, methods for detection
of OTA include TLC, HPLC, ELISA, and GICA. Currently,
HPLC-based methods are most commonly used for
detection of OTA, with HPLC-MS/MS utilised often
(Chen et al. 2011; Kuang and Qiu 2012b). In 2010, Yang
et al. (2010) established the ﬁrst HPLC-FLD method for
detecting and quantifying OTA contamination levels in
CHMs in China. Since then, HPLC-FLD has been routinely
used to determine OTA levels in herbal medicines

4. Zearalenone
Zearalenone (ZEN) is an oestrogen-like mycotoxin
produced mainly by Fusarium graminearum and
F. oxysporum. Studies have shown that ZEN is
a reproductive toxin and that exposure to ZEN has
teratogenic eﬀects. At concentrations of 1 nmol∙L−1–
10 nmol∙L−1, ZEN can stimulate the transcription of
oestrogen receptors and aﬀect cell division and
growth (Deng and Yuan 2007). ZEN is also able to
cause DNA damage, inhibit protein and DNA synth-
esis, and interfere with the cell cycle to block DNA
replication and inhibit cell proliferation; high doses of
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
interfere with the cell cycle to block DNA
replication and inhibit cell proliferation; high doses of
ZEN can induce damage to the immune system as
well (Jiang et al. 2011).

4.2. ZEN contaminants in CHMs
A study of the prevalence of ZEN contamination in
105 diﬀerent CHMs revealed that 41 of them were
contaminated by ZEN (per cent positive rate was
39%), and level of ZEN contamination ranged from
0.2 to 931.07 μg∙kg−1 (Table 5). Some reports have
shown that seed fruits such as S. Coicis (Yang et al.
2011c; Kong et al. 2013) and S. Persicae (Han 2011) are
easily contaminated by ZEN; in the case of S. Coicis,
the ZEN-positive detection rate is as high as 83%. ZEN
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
ontaminated by ZEN; in the case of S. Coicis,
the ZEN-positive detection rate is as high as 83%. ZEN
has been detected as a contaminant in roots, rhi-
zomes, leaves, and in the case of one study, in the
cortex of the herb Juniperus procumbens (Han et al.
2012), at a level of 2.3 μg∙kg−1. A very high level of ZEN
was reportedly detected in Cistanche tubulosa, but
due to the small number of samples, this ﬁnding
bears additional exploration (Yang et al. 2011c).
5. Other mycotoxins
Although AFs and OTA are the most commonly
reported mycotoxin contaminants, occurrence of
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
mycotoxins
Although AFs and OTA are the most commonly
reported mycotoxin contaminants, occurrence of
other mycotoxins such as fumonisins, trichothecenes,
citrinin, and patulin has also been described in CHMs.
Fumonisin is a type of secondary metabolite pro-
duced by F. oxysporum and includes the A, B, C, P and
FB1 derivatives. In 1993, it was classiﬁed as a Class
B
carcinogen
by
the
International
Agency
for
Research on Cancer. Fumonisin mainly damages the
heart, liver, lungs, kidneys and other organs of animals,
and exposure to fumonisin can result in porcine pul-
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
er, lungs, kidneys and other organs of animals,
and exposure to fumonisin can result in porcine pul-
monary oedema, liver damage, cardiovascular disease,
and equine leukoencephalomalacia. In addition, expo-
sure to fumonisin may cause human oesophageal can-
cer and neural tube defects (Yang et al. 2014a).
Trichothecenes is a class of secondary metabolites
produced by diﬀerent Fusarium species, such as
F. graminearum and F. serrata; compounds in this
group include T-2 toxin, deoxynivalenol (DON), niva-
lenol (NIV), diacetoxyscirpenol (DAS), and its deriva-
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
nclude T-2 toxin, deoxynivalenol (DON), niva-
lenol (NIV), diacetoxyscirpenol (DAS), and its deriva-
tives (Yue 2009). Studies have shown that T-2 toxin is
one of the most toxic mycotoxins among the type-A
trichothecene mycotoxins. T-2 toxin can inhibit the
synthesis of cellular proteins, DNA and RNA, trigger
DNA damage via oxidative stress, induce apoptosis,
alter gene expression patterns, and damage the cell
membrane. T-2 toxin can also cause pathological
changes in liver tissue and damage to the immune
system (Zhou et al. 2011). DON, also called vomiting
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
hanges in liver tissue and damage to the immune
system (Zhou et al. 2011). DON, also called vomiting
toxin, is highly cytotoxic, induces apoptosis, inhibits
proliferation of immune cells, induces cytokine pro-
duction from helper T-cells, and activates macro-
phages and T-cells, resulting in additional cytokine
production (Huo et al. 2008).
Citrinin is a mycotoxin produced by ﬁlamentous
fungi
including
Penicillium,
Aspergillus,
and
Monascus. As a nephrotoxin, citrinin exposure can
cause kidney disease in a variety of animals such as
dogs, pigs, rats, chickens, and birds. Citrinin exposure
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
ney disease in a variety of animals such as
dogs, pigs, rats, chickens, and birds. Citrinin exposure
can also induce mutations and result in deformities
and tumours (Li et al. 2011b). Furthermore, the eﬀects
of citrinin can synergise with other mycotoxins (such
as ochratoxin and patulin) to inﬂict more deleterious
eﬀects to tissues and organs (Liu and Xu 2004).
Patulin is a genotoxic compound that has been
found to have broad toxicity and exposure to patulin
can cause a variety of symptoms in humans and
animals, including nausea, vomiting, blood in the
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
ulin
can cause a variety of symptoms in humans and
animals, including nausea, vomiting, blood in the
stool, convulsions, and coma (Zhou et al. 2010). In
addition, patulin exposure can result in acute and
subacute poisoning. Furthermore, exposure to patulin
has been reported to have cytotoxic, teratogenic,
carcinogenic, and immunotoxic eﬀects.
5.1. Detection methods for other mycotoxins
Fumonisin is currently detected using HPLC-MS/MS. In
2011, the method for simultaneously detecting fumoni-
sin B1 (FB1) and fumonisin B2 (FB2) in 34 types of CHMs

chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
method for simultaneously detecting fumoni-
sin B1 (FB1) and fumonisin B2 (FB2) in 34 types of CHMs
was developed by Xie et al. (2011). An immunoaﬃnity
column was used to purify samples and the detection
limit for FB1 and FB2 with this approach was 2 μg∙kg−1.
A method to detect T-2 toxin contamination in
CHMs using GC with ECD (GC-ECD) was ﬁrst proposed
by Yue et al. (2009). In order to improve the selectivity
and sensitivity of the method, sample clean-up was
performed using an immunoaﬃnity column, and

5.2. Other mycotoxin contaminants in CHMs
Mycotoxins such as FB, T-2 toxin, and DON have been
successfully detected in CHMs (Table 6). For example, the
fruit and seeds of CHMs such as S. Sterculiae Lychnophorae
and S. Coicis are susceptible to fumonisin B contamination.

Along with a variety of methods for detecting diﬀer-
ent mycotoxins, methods for simultaneous determina-
tion for various mycotoxins have been gradually
developed. AFB1 and OTA contaminants in CHMs can
be detected together by HPLC-FLD, with use of
a composite immunoaﬃnity column for sample cleanup
(Wei et al. 2011; Cao et al. 2013). Furthermore, simulta-
neous detection of DON and NIV in CHMs by HPLC-UV

was ﬁrst proposed by Yue et al. (2010b). The sample pre-
treatment procedure used in this work abolished the
derivatisation step used in the conventional approach to
yield improved results. Several years later, Kong et al.
(2012) developed a method for simultaneously measur-
ing T-2 and HT-2 toxins in CHMs.
With the spread of modern MS technology, new
methods for the combined detection of mycotoxins
with large chemical diversity continue to be developed

hods for the combined detection of mycotoxins
with large chemical diversity continue to be developed
and applied. At present, it has been demonstrated that
up to 35 diﬀerent toxins can be detected from an herbal
matrix in a single HPLC-MS/MS run (Han et al. 2012).
7. Conclusion
At present, mycotoxin contaminants have become
some of the most prevalent hazardous substances in
CHMs and a major public safety concern regarding
their sale and use. In this review, we summarised
some common mycotoxin contaminants found in
medicinal materials and discussed methods for their
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
ised
some common mycotoxin contaminants found in
medicinal materials and discussed methods for their
detection. Mycotoxin contamination is usually hetero-
geneous, so screening methods for detecting these
contaminants in medicinal products need to have
broad coverage across, and samples should be pro-
cessed carefully (Zhang et al. 2018a; Tittlemier et al.
2019). However, many existing studies of mycotoxin
contamination lack detailed descriptions of how
samples are selected and processed. To guarantee
an accurate snapshot of any existing mycotoxin con-
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
samples are selected and processed. To guarantee
an accurate snapshot of any existing mycotoxin con-
taminants, careful considerations need to be taken
with regard to sample acquisition and processing.
Another complication in collecting accurate data lies
in that the rapid detection methods such as ELISA and
GICA are more prone to false negatives or false posi-
tives
than
conventional
detection
methods.
Therefore, further validation should be performed
on any signiﬁcant ﬁndings that rely on rapid detection
methods. In addition, the mycotoxin contamination is
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
signiﬁcant ﬁndings that rely on rapid detection
methods. In addition, the mycotoxin contamination is
a known problem in Chinese herbal medicines. For
example, S. Platycladi and S. Ziziphi Spinosae are prone
to aﬂatoxin contamination, Glycyrrhiza uralensis and
Zingiber Oﬃcinale Roscoe are prone to OTA contam-
ination, and ZEN contamination is prevalent in
S. Coicis and R. Paeoniae alba. In some medicines,
such as S. Persicae and Polygonum multiﬂorum, co-
occurrence of multiple mycotoxin contaminations
had been detected.
Although some producers of CHMs currently have
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
multiple mycotoxin contaminations
had been detected.
Although some producers of CHMs currently have
some standards in place for monitoring the levels of
mycotoxins such as AFs and OTA, standardised guide-
lines regarding monitoring for other mycotoxins and
their levels have not been established for CHMs.
Therefore, it is necessary to conduct additional
research to better understand which CHMs are easily
contaminated by which mycotoxins. This information
can then be used to establish guidelines for screening
for mycotoxin contaminants and limitations on accep-
table levels in CHMs.

chunks.text:
guidelines for screening
for mycotoxin contaminants and limitations on accep-
table levels in CHMs.
Rapid analytical methods for mycotoxin detection are
currently under development and are increasingly uti-
lised by CHM producers. In recent years, standard biolo-
gical analysis methods have been utilised for detection of
mycotoxins in CHMs; such methods include the GCIA and
ELISA approaches. Novel technologies such as ultrasensi-
tive mycotoxin biosensors have been developed and
utilised for mycotoxin screening in food and serum. For
example, Taghdisi et al. (Taghdisi et al. 2016) developed
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
mycotoxin screening in food and serum. For
example, Taghdisi et al. (Taghdisi et al. 2016) developed
a ﬂuorescent aptamer sensor (aptasensor) that allowed
for selective and sensitive detection of OTA in grape juice
and serum. Since then, this group has proposed another
accurate ﬂuorescent sensing method for the determina-
tion of AFB1 in grape juice and human serum samples
based on a hairpin structure of a G-quadruplex oligonu-
cleotide-aptamer chimera (Taghdisi et al. 2018). A highly
sensitive aptasensor utilising the ﬂuorescence resonance
energy transfer for AFM1 detection in milk samples was
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
ptasensor utilising the ﬂuorescence resonance
energy transfer for AFM1 detection in milk samples was

recently developed (Li et al. 2017a). Another group estab-
lished a surface plasmon resonance (SPR) method using
an SPR sensor chip for simultaneous detection of AFB1,
OTA, ZEN, and DON in corn (Wei et al. 2019). However,
broad application of these recently developed mycotoxin
detection methods in CHMs requires further validation.
In recent years, studies on the presence of myco-
toxin contaminants in CHMs have mainly focused on

chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
In recent years, studies on the presence of myco-
toxin contaminants in CHMs have mainly focused on
identifying the varieties of mycotoxins present, deter-
mining the contamination level, and reﬁning myco-
toxin detection methods. In contrast, relatively few
studies have examined these mycotoxin contamina-
tions in the context of toxigenic mechanisms, detox-
iﬁcation techniques, and prevention and control
measures. The presence of speciﬁc mycotoxin con-
taminants and their relative abundance in medicinal
materials is intimately related to the place of origin,
processing
methods,
and
storage
chunks.title: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines
chunks.filename: Occurrence and analysis of mycotoxins in domestic Chinese herbal medicines.pdf

chunks.text:
in medicinal
materials is intimately related to the place of origin,
processing
methods,
and
storage
conditions.
Therefore, future studies should focus on investigat-
ing the occurrence of mycotoxin contamination in
CHMs in various storage conditions, and ﬁndings
from these studies can be used to help establish an
eﬃcient prevention strategy to minimise the pre-
sence of fungi and mycotoxin contaminants in CHMs.

【中文摘要】Protection of Prenylated Flavonoids from Mori Cortex Radicis (Moraceae)
标题：桑白皮（Mori Cortex Radicis）中异戊烯基黄酮类化合物对一氧化氮诱导的神经母细胞瘤SH-SY5Y细胞死亡的保护作用
关键词：桑白皮，桑根皮，异戊烯基黄酮，异戊烯基黄酮醇，异戊烯基二氢黄酮，桑酮，桑黄酮，神经保护，一氧化氮，硝基氧化应激，SH-SY5Y细胞，MTT法
摘要：从桑白皮（桑根皮）甲醇提取物中分离得到7个异戊烯基黄酮类化合物（licoflavone C、cyclomulberrin、neocyclomorusin、sanggenon I、morusin、kuwanon U、kuwanon E）和3个2-芳基苯并呋喃类化合物（moracin P、moracin O、mulberrofuran Q），采用MTT还原法评估其对硝普钠诱导的SH-SY5Y神经母细胞瘤细胞死亡的保护作用。结果显示，C-3位异戊烯基黄酮（cyclomulberrin、neocyclomorusin、morusin）和异戊烯基二氢黄酮（sanggenon I、kuwanon U、kuwanon E）呈剂量依赖性增强细胞活力，而缺乏C-3异戊烯基的licoflavone C及2-芳基苯并呋喃类化合物无保护作用，表明部分异戊烯基黄酮类成分可能通过抑制硝基氧化应激介导的细胞死亡发挥神经保护作用。

used in oriental medicine as an antidiabetic, a diure-
tic, an expectorant and a laxative agent (Yadav and
Nade, 2008). It has been mainly used for the treatment
of constipation, cough, dizziness and urinary inconti-
nence. And it has been used to treat fever, protect the
liver, improve eyesight, strengthen joints, discharge of
urine and lower blood pressure and protect from
neuronal damages (Katsube et al., 2010). A number of
prenylated flavonoids, stilbenes, benzofurans, terpenes,
alkaloids, and other phenolic compounds were pre-

Nitrosative stress is the state of overproduction of
reactive nitrogen species (Klatt et al., 2000; Ridnour

et al., 2005). Nitrosative stress may lead to alteration
of the protein structure by nitrosylation reactions, and
inhibit their normal function, causing cell death
(Valko et al., 2007).
Nitric oxide has been implicated as an important
mediator of both acute and chronic neurodegenerative
injuries (Dawson and Dawson, 1996; Hantraye et al.,
1996; Heales et al., 1999). For example, inhibitors of
neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS) have been shown

tion against cerebral ischemia (Huang et al., 1994).
And also it contributes to misfolding and accumulat-
ing proteins in a number of neurodegenerative disorders
including Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease,
amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and polyglutamine dis-

In this present study, we investigated whether com-

It is well reported that NO is the molecule respon-
sible for a lot of pharmacological and toxicological
effects elicited by SNP (Cardaci et al., 2008). NO and
its metabolites were found to induce apoptotic cell death
both in neuronal cell lines and in primary neurons
(Zhang and Zhao, 2003). Also, NO is a main factor
contributing to damages in neuronal sites in ischemic

chunks.text:
ang and Zhao, 2003). Also, NO is a main factor
contributing to damages in neuronal sites in ischemic
stroke, demyelinating diseases and other neurode-
generative disorders (Lim et al., 2009).
In our search for neuroprotective agents of natural
origin, a MeOH extract of Mori Cortex Radicis signifi-
cantly increased the cell viability of SH-SY5Y human
neuroblastoma cells exposed to SNP (EC50 39.2 µg/
mL). Bioactivity-guided fractionation of the MeOH
extract of Mori Cortex Radicis using this assay led to
the isolation of ten known compounds (1-10).
Among the tested compounds, C-3 prenylated fla-

Among the tested compounds, C-3 prenylated fla-

morusin (5), improved cell viability in dose-dependent
manner against SNP-induced cell death in SH-SY5Y
cells, with an EC50 values of 4.4, 5.6, and 6.4 µg/mL,
respectively. Also, prenylated flavanones, sanggenon I
(4), kuwanons U (6), and E (7), exhibited inhibitory
activity, with an EC50 values ranging 7.9 to 12.0 µg/
mL. However, licoflavone (1, which lacks the prenyl
group at C-3) and three 2-arylbenzofurans (8-10) did

Although further extensive studies regarding the
effects of these compounds from Mori Cortex Radicis
on nitrosative stress-mediated diseases are necessary,
we expect some prenylated flavonoids from Mori

【中文摘要】Quantitative Comparison of the Marker Compounds in Different Medicinal Parts of Morus alba L. Using High-Performance Liquid Chromatography-Diode Array Detector with Chemometric Analysis
标题：桑（桑白皮、桑枝、桑叶、桑椹）不同药用部位标志化合物的定量比较：高效液相色谱-二极管阵列检测器结合化学计量学分析
关键词：桑（Morus alba L.），桑白皮，桑枝，桑叶，桑椹，标志化合物，黄酮类，芪类，酚酸，香豆素，高效液相色谱-二极管阵列检测器（HPLC-DAD），化学计量学，主成分分析（PCA），热图分析，定量分析
摘要：本研究采用高效液相色谱-二极管阵列检测器（HPLC-DAD）结合化学计量学（主成分分析和热图分析），对桑（Morus alba L.）的57个样品（15个桑白皮、11个桑枝、12个桑椹、19个桑叶）中12种标志化合物（包括7种黄酮类、2种芪类、2种酚酸和1种香豆素）进行定量比较。结果显示，各药用部位中标志化合物的含量和组成存在显著差异：桑叶中6种化合物含量较高，桑白皮中4种化合物含量较高，桑枝中2种化合物含量较高；化学计量学分析表明样品按药用部位聚类，桑白皮与桑皮苷A、花旗松素、桑黄酮G和桑酮相关，桑枝与4-羟基肉桂酸和氧化白藜芦醇相关，桑叶与东莨菪苷、绿原酸、芦丁、异槲皮苷、紫云英苷和槲皮苷相关。

Abstract: It is thought that the therapeutic eﬃcacy of Morus alba L. is determined by its biological
compounds. We investigated the chemical diﬀerences in the medicinal parts of M. alba by analyzing a
total of 57 samples (15 root barks, 11 twigs, 12 fruits, and 19 leaves). Twelve marker compounds,
including seven ﬂavonoids, two stilbenoids, two phenolic acids, and a coumarin, were quantitatively
analyzed using a high-performance liquid chromatography-diode array detector and chemometric
analyses (principal component and heatmap analysis). The results demonstrated that the levels and

pigment development, fruit development, and ripening, or allelopathy [13–16]. Hence, determining

3. Discussion
The phytochemical levels, particularly the secondary metabolites, showed part-speciﬁc or
tissue-speciﬁc variation of single plants, which corresponds to the fact that gene expression for
phytochemical biosynthesis is highly plant-part dependent [24–26]. However, some compounds
represented signiﬁcant variations of the contents even in same medicinal part, presumably due

pounds
represented signiﬁcant variations of the contents even in same medicinal part, presumably due
to intra-species factors (i.e., diﬀerent levels of the secondary metabolite biosynthesis, deposit or
transformation) or extrinsic factors (i.e., circumstance of growing, harvesting season, degree of sample
dryness, etc.).
In our ﬁndings, chlorogenic acid (3-caﬀeoylquinic acid) was found at the highest amount in
M. alba leaves, followed by rutin (quercetin-3-O-rutinoside) and isoquercitrin (quercetin-3-O-glucoside),

as previously reported [27,28]. Chlorogenic acid is preferentially formed in the leaves of M. alba
by shikimate/quinate hydroxycinnamoyltransferase (HCT), particularly MaHCT4, during the

Isoquercitrin is derived from quercetin primarily in

rutin via ﬂavonol-3-O-glucoside-L-rhamnosyltransferase (UGT78D1), particularly MaUGT78D1,

The quantitative analysis of the marker compounds was performed using an Agilent 1260 liquid
chromatography system (Agilent Technologies, Palo Alto, CA, USA) equipped with an autosampler,
degasser, quaternary solvent pump, and diode array detector. Data was processed using ChemStation
software (Agilent Technologies Inc., USA). Twelve marker compounds were separated on a Capcell

4.5. Chemometric Statistical Analysis
The distributions of the Morus samples and their marker compounds were analyzed, then visualized
using the chemometric tools. A matrix consisting of rows (Morus samples) and columns (marker
compound contents) was used to perform the chemometric analyses. The quantitative diﬀerences in
the 12 marker compounds were compared using the Tukey’s test. The diﬀerences were considered

statistically signiﬁcant at p < 0.05, p < 0.01 or p < 0.001. The Tukey’s test and chemometric analyses
were performed using open-source software R (v. 4.0.2; The R Foundation for Statistical Computing).

【中文摘要】Recent Advances on the Chemical Composition, Pharmacological Properties, and Product Development of Morus alba
标题：桑（桑白皮）化学成分、药理活性及产品开发研究进展

关键词：桑，桑白皮，桑枝，桑叶，桑葚，黄酮类，生物碱，抗糖尿病，抗肿瘤，抗氧化，抗菌，化学成分，药理活性，产品开发，综述

摘要：本文综述了桑（Morus alba）的桑枝、桑果（桑葚）、桑叶及根皮（桑白皮）等不同药用部位的化学成分、药理活性及产品开发进展。桑富含黄酮类、生物碱等多种活性成分，具有抗糖尿病、抗肿瘤、抗氧化及抗菌等药理作用，已广泛应用于功能性食品和健康产品开发。

ABSTRACT
Introduction: Morus alba, a member of the Moraceae family, has a long history of medicinal use in China. Its branches, fruits,
leaves, and root bark are rich in various bioactive compounds, including flavonoids, alkaloids, and other phytochemicals. These
plant parts exhibit a broad spectrum of pharmacological activities, such as antidiabetic, antitumor, antibacterial, and antiox-
chunks.title: Recent Advances on the Chemical Composition, Pharmacological Properties, and Product Development of Morus alba
chunks.filename: Recent Advances on the Chemical CompositionPharmacological Properties and Produ.pdf

chunks.text:
spectrum of pharmacological activities, such as antidiabetic, antitumor, antibacterial, and antiox-
idant effects. Owing to these properties, various parts of M. alba have been developed into functional foods and health prod-
ucts, attracting considerable public and scientific interest. Objectives: This review aims to summarize current knowledge on
the phytochemistry, pharmacological activities, and product development related to different parts of M. alba, with particular
chunks.title: Recent Advances on the Chemical Composition, Pharmacological Properties, and Product Development of Morus alba
chunks.filename: Recent Advances on the Chemical CompositionPharmacological Properties and Produ.pdf

chunks.text:
cological activities, and product development related to different parts of M. alba, with particular
emphasis on their respective roles in the development of functional products. Methods: Relevant literature was retrieved from
major scientific databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. Information related to the
phytochemistry, pharmacological effects, and product development of various parts of M. alba was systematically collected and
chunks.title: Recent Advances on the Chemical Composition, Pharmacological Properties, and Product Development of Morus alba
chunks.filename: Recent Advances on the Chemical CompositionPharmacological Properties and Produ.pdf

chunks.text:
ogical effects, and product development of various parts of M. alba was systematically collected and
analyzed. Results: This review summarizes the chemical composition of different parts of M. alba and their corresponding phar-
macological properties. It also highlights recent advancements in the development of functional products derived from M. alba.
Conclusions: M.orus alba contains a wide array of bioactive compounds with promising pharmacological potential. Its various
parts have demonstrated potential in the prevention and management of chronic diseases and have been increasingly utilized
chunks.title: Recent Advances on the Chemical Composition, Pharmacological Properties, and Product Development of Morus alba
chunks.filename: Recent Advances on the Chemical CompositionPharmacological Properties and Produ.pdf

chunks.text:
d potential in the prevention and management of chronic diseases and have been increasingly utilized
in the development of functional health products. Further interdisciplinary studies are warranted to facilitate its translational
application in modern healthcare.
1   |   Introduction
Morus alba, a member of the Moraceae family, is a peren-
nial deciduous tree or shrub widely distributed across Asia,
Africa, Europe, Oceania, and other regions, with particular
prevalence in Asia [1]. As one of the earliest countries to cul-
tivate M. alba, China has a long history of M. alba cultivation.
chunks.title: Recent Advances on the Chemical Composition, Pharmacological Properties, and Product Development of Morus alba
chunks.filename: Recent Advances on the Chemical CompositionPharmacological Properties and Produ.pdf

chunks.text:
e of the earliest countries to cul-
tivate M. alba, China has a long history of M. alba cultivation.
Furthermore, China is home to one of the richest diversities of
